Source for the EchoXIV suite of FFXIV Dalamud plugins. # EchoXIV

Source for the EchoXIV plugins for FINAL FANTASY XIV, one directory each.

| | |
|---|---|
| [EchoGlam](EchoGlam/) | Build glamours from every item in the game, save them as outfits, and publish them to a catalogue anybody can wear from |
| [EchoMix](EchoMix/) | A two-deck DJ booth with live mixing, a playlist library, and broadcasts other players can tune into in-game or from a browser |
| [EchoNav](EchoNav/) | Lists the Critical Encounters and FATEs running in Occult Crescent: North Horn and walks you to any of them |
| [EchoRoleplay](EchoRoleplay/) | A roleplay profile for your character, readable by anybody who hovers them, with statuses and private notes |
| [EchoSim](EchoSim/) | Simulates a full fight for twenty-one jobs, compares gear and melds against the result, and scores your real kills on per-job leaderboards |

More will appear here as they are opened up.

## Installing

The plugins are not distributed from this repository. Add this to Dalamud's custom plugin
repositories:

```
https://echoxiv.com/pluginmaster.json
```

Then install from Dalamud's plugin installer as usual. [echoxiv.com](https://echoxiv.com) has a page
for each plugin with what it does and what it looks like.

## What Is Here

The source for each shipped release, kept in step with the binary that was published. Each plugin
directory carries its own `LICENSE`, `README.md` and `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`, because the plugins do
not all depend on the same third-party work and the notices belong with the code they describe.

## Licence

Each plugin states its own licence in its directory. All of them link against
[Dalamud](https://github.com/goatcorp/Dalamud), which is AGPL-3.0, and are licensed accordingly.

with or endorsement by Square Enix.

variant.changelog:
Added:

The live score has a bar under the number, filled to your score, so it reads at a glance without you having to look straight at it.

You can set how big the live score is drawn - Small, Medium or Large - under Settings, Live Score.

Settings has an About tab, showing your EchoSim, game and Dalamud versions.

The timeline has minute markers, so you can find a point in a long fight without scrolling past every row on the way to it.

The burst chart has axes.

Your profile's older eras can be collapsed.

The leaderboards tell you what happened to your last submitted kill.

Changed:

The interface has been rebuilt. Nine tabs are now four pages - Build, Result, Analyse and Compete - with Settings behind the cog, and the job you are simulating, the Run button, the status line and your DPS sit in a bar along the bottom that is there whichever page you are on.

The window is one fixed size, chosen to fit the pages, and the two size sliders are gone.

The row of job icons is gone. The job you are simulating is a chip at the bottom left - click it to pick another.

Fight length, potion timings and target count are one control each, rather than a slider, a typed box and a row of preset buttons between them.

Settings is four tabs: Appearance, Live Score, About and Changelog.

Appearance offers thirty-one colour schemes in seven groups, including EchoMix's and EchoGlam's own, where there used to be five.

Reporting a bug has moved into Settings, About. It used to be a button in the window's corner.

Live Score is no longer marked beta. What the badge was there to say is said plainly instead: a job's modelled ceiling is corrected whenever a submission shows it is wrong, and every score measured against it moves when it is. That is how it works rather than a phase it is passing through.

The leaderboards now have seasons, and the boards you have been climbing were the beta. It closed on 8 September, when patch 7.56 enabled the Echo in AAC Heavyweight - so those standings are final, and whoever was on a board then keeps that rank and score permanently. Season 1 begins with Evercold.

Scores set since the beta closed are still kept, verified and shown to you on the board and your profile, marked out of season. They are not ranked.

There is one leaderboard per fight holding every job, instead of one per job. A filter on the board puts it back to your job alone, and your title is still awarded on your rank among players of your own job.

Your profile is a list of fights rather than a grid of tiles, so the scores read down one column.

The leaderboards and your profile say what the score is measured against. The number used to sit under a column headed Score with no scale anywhere on the page, which invited reading it as an FFLogs percentile.

Analyse says which of its three steps you are on, and leads with your parse.

Analyse shows one finding at a time with its explanation beside the list. Every finding used to show its whole explanation at once.

Gear Compare's headline percentage is labelled a stat weight estimate. It was presented as expected damage, which is more than that figure can support - it has no rotation and no raid buffs in it, and it can read a set worse than your own gear while winning a real simulation.

Best in Slot simulates both a set that reaches your job's speed tier and one that spends nothing on speed, and keeps whichever does more damage. It used to buy the tier whatever it cost.

Changing page is quicker. It used to hold the page you had just left for a moment before showing the one you asked for.

This changelog is grouped into Added, Changed and Fixed, and the older entries have been rewritten to match. Nothing was dropped from them.

Fixed:

Analyse now names the job on a parse for a job EchoSim does not simulate. It was printing FFLogs' own spelling - DarkKnight - beside a blank icon.

The live score no longer reads "no simulation for this job yet" for a job it does simulate, which it did for the first moments of every pull after you changed job.

The live score panel no longer resizes itself. It grew a line whenever a phase transition paused it, and changed shape again on a job it cannot score.

The live score's hundredths could read 97 for a score of 98.

The live score follows your font scale. It stayed the same pixel size however large the rest of the plugin was.

The window no longer opens larger than your screen, and no longer reopens off the edge of it after you change resolution.

A page that fails no longer takes the rest of the window with it. The other pages, the Run button and the bug report all stay available.

Best in Slot no longer logs warnings about your relic having no substats and your gear having empty sockets while it is part way through building a set.

A Sage record on M3S that a later kill had overwritten is back on the board.

Added:

The live score has a bar under the number, filled to your score, so it reads at a glance without you having to look straight at it.

You can set how big the live score is drawn - Small, Medium or Large - under Settings, Live Score.

Settings has an About tab, showing your EchoSim, game and Dalamud versions.

The timeline has minute markers, so you can find a point in a long fight without scrolling past every row on the way to it.

The burst chart has axes.

Your profile's older eras can be collapsed.

The leaderboards tell you what happened to your last submitted kill.

Changed:

The interface has been rebuilt. Nine tabs are now four pages - Build, Result, Analyse and Compete - with Settings behind the cog, and the job you are simulating, the Run button, the status line and your DPS sit in a bar along the bottom that is there whichever page you are on.

The window is one fixed size, chosen to fit the pages, and the two size sliders are gone.

The row of job icons is gone. The job you are simulating is a chip at the bottom left - click it to pick another.

Fight length, potion timings and target count are one control each, rather than a slider, a typed box and a row of preset buttons between them.

Settings is four tabs: Appearance, Live Score, About and Changelog.

Appearance offers thirty-one colour schemes in seven groups, including EchoMix's and EchoGlam's own, where there used to be five.

Reporting a bug has moved into Settings, About. It used to be a button in the window's corner.

Live Score is no longer marked beta. What the badge was there to say is said plainly instead: a job's modelled ceiling is corrected whenever a submission shows it is wrong, and every score measured against it moves when it is. That is how it works rather than a phase it is passing through.

The leaderboards now have seasons, and the boards you have been climbing were the beta. It closed on 8 September, when patch 7.56 enabled the Echo in AAC Heavyweight - so those standings are final, and whoever was on a board then keeps that rank and score permanently. Season 1 begins with Evercold.

Scores set since the beta closed are still kept, verified and shown to you on the board and your profile, marked out of season. They are not ranked.

There is one leaderboard per fight holding every job, instead of one per job. A filter on the board puts it back to your job alone, and your title is still awarded on your rank among players of your own job.

Your profile is a list of fights rather than a grid of tiles, so the scores read down one column.

The leaderboards and your profile say what the score is measured against. The number used to sit under a column headed Score with no scale anywhere on the page, which invited reading it as an FFLogs percentile.

Analyse says which of its three steps you are on, and leads with your parse.

Analyse shows one finding at a time with its explanation beside the list. Every finding used to show its whole explanation at once.

Gear Compare's headline percentage is labelled a stat weight estimate. It was presented as expected damage, which is more than that figure can support - it has no rotation and no raid buffs in it, and it can read a set worse than your own gear while winning a real simulation.

Best in Slot simulates both a set that reaches your job's speed tier and one that spends nothing on speed, and keeps whichever does more damage. It used to buy the tier whatever it cost.

Changing page is quicker. It used to hold the page you had just left for a moment before showing the one you asked for.

This changelog is grouped into Added, Changed and Fixed, and the older entries have been rewritten to match. Nothing was dropped from them.

Fixed:

Analyse now names the job on a parse for a job EchoSim does not simulate. It was printing FFLogs' own spelling - DarkKnight - beside a blank icon.

The live score no longer reads "no simulation for this job yet" for a job it does simulate, which it did for the first moments of every pull after you changed job.

The live score panel no longer resizes itself. It grew a line whenever a phase transition paused it, and changed shape again on a job it cannot score.

The live score's hundredths could read 97 for a score of 98.

The live score follows your font scale. It stayed the same pixel size however large the rest of the plugin was.

The window no longer opens larger than your screen, and no longer reopens off the edge of it after you change resolution.

A page that fails no longer takes the rest of the window with it. The other pages, the Run button and the bug report all stay available.

Best in Slot no longer logs warnings about your relic having no substats and your gear having empty sockets while it is part way through building a set.

A Sage record on M3S that a later kill had overwritten is back on the board.
